---

# Regulatory memo: HR assistant (Érable Logistics)

> **Drafting aid output, not legal advice.** Prepared to support the
> reviewer named in `for:`, never to replace the client's lawyer. It is not
> reviewed until that reviewer records a decision in Review and sign-off at
> the end; counsel decides every legal conclusion in it.

Draft for Érable Logistics' counsel. It records which regimes the jurisdiction
screen found in scope, the facts the design records, and the provisions that
appear relevant in Australia (through the consultancy's own handling) and in
Canada (Quebec and Ontario), neither of which has an AI Act or assigns a risk
tier. Conclusions are proposals for counsel; not legal advice. This run was
non-interactive: each question the drafter would have asked is written under
Questions for counsel, with the assumption proceeded on.

## Summary

- **Direct question: does Law 25 apply to the leave decisions?** counsel: proposed answer, yes for Montréal staff and in two layers. (1) Quebec's private sector Act as amended by Law 25 is proposed to govern Érable's handling of Montréal staff personal information, because Érable's head office is in Montréal and 1,150 staff work there (docs/discovery/hr-assistant.md §1; canada.md reference says the Act covers a Quebec enterprise's employees, checked 2026-10-26). (2) Section 12.1 (decisions based exclusively on automated processing) is proposed to be engaged for auto-approved requests from Quebec staff, because a code rule decides and no person reviews (C3, C4, D5; M2 shows 64% of pilot-shape requests would be decided that way). It is proposed not engaged for requests routed to the manager (C5), where a person decides. The text of s 12.1 is reported; not confirmed at the source on 2026-10-26. Two points decide it and are for counsel: whether a deterministic rule is "automated processing", and whether a favourable decision (an approval) is covered (Questions 1 and 2).
- **Law 25 duties that apply whatever the answer on s 12.1:** counsel: the s 3.3 privacy impact assessment for the project, the s 17 assessment and written agreement for every flow leaving Quebec (Toronto hosting, US model processing, Sydney log access: D1, D2, D4), the s 3.1 person in charge, and the confidentiality incident duties (docs/discovery/hr-assistant.md §5; checked 2026-10-26).
- **Regimes in scope:** Australia (through the consultancy's own handling only) and Canada (Quebec and Ontario). United States, EU, United Kingdom, New Zealand and Singapore are out, each with its reason in the screen (counsel: confirm the screen).
- **Main obligations in each regime:** Canada: Quebec s 3.3 and s 17 assessments, s 12.1 notice, explanation and review route (C3, C4; checked 2026-10-26), and for Ontario staff no general private sector privacy statute but the electronic monitoring policy and human rights duties (D3; checked 2026-10-26). Australia: whether the Privacy Act reaches the consultancy's Sydney access, and APP 11 and notifiable data breach duties if it does (D4; counsel).
- **Proposed roles:** Érable is the enterprise responsible for the personal information; Southgate Labs and Google Cloud handle it for Érable (Roles below; counsel: confirm).
- **Biggest facts not in the record:** no employee notice, no Quebec EFVP or s 17 assessment, no written agreement covering Sydney access or Google, no review or explanation route for auto-approved requests, no screening of leave reasons that may mention health, no model retirement date (gap: each listed under Questions for counsel and proposed as goals).
- **Blocking questions:** counsel: 12 questions, 9 of them needed before the pilot decision on 2026-11-24 (docs/discovery/hr-assistant.md §6), listed under Questions for counsel.

## Jurisdiction screen

| Regime | In scope | Trigger facts | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Australia | yes | Southgate Labs engineers in Sydney read logs holding prompts and employee IDs during the pilot and a three-month support period (D4); consultancy home assumed Australia (assumption: default, no other home stated) | The consultancy's own handling only; counsel: whether the Privacy Act reaches that handling of Canadian staff data. The client's own APP 1.7 and sector rows are n/a: client and data subjects are in Canada |
| United States | no | Staff are in Montréal and Toronto only (docs/discovery/hr-assistant.md §1); Gemini processing in the United States is a processing location (D1) | n/a: no US client, resident or purpose; data merely processed in the US is a transfer fact for the Canadian sections, not a trigger |
| EU | no | No EU establishment, people or output use (docs/discovery/hr-assistant.md §1) | n/a: nothing brings the AI Act or GDPR in |
| United Kingdom | no | No UK establishment or people (docs/discovery/hr-assistant.md §1) | n/a: nothing brings UK GDPR in |
| New Zealand | no | No New Zealand client, staff or data (docs/discovery/hr-assistant.md §1) | n/a: nothing brings the Privacy Act 2020 in |
| Singapore | no | No Singapore client, staff or data (docs/discovery/hr-assistant.md §1) | n/a: nothing brings the PDPA in |
| Canada | yes | Provincially regulated employer headquartered in Montréal with 1,150 Montréal and 640 Toronto staff (docs/discovery/hr-assistant.md §1); real employee and leave data (docs/architecture/hr-assistant.md Scope gate) | Quebec enterprise with Quebec staff; Ontario staff as a separate flow; which law governs each flow is counsel: |

- **Processing locations:** Cloud Run, Cloud SQL and logs in northamerica-northeast2 (Toronto) (D2); Gemini 3.5 Flash through the Vertex AI global endpoint, with processing in the United States per the model page, read 2026-09-10 (D1; not re-read in this run, no network); abuse monitoring, grounding and telemetry sinks (gap: not recorded in the design); Southgate Labs engineers read logs from Sydney (D4; gap: how and from where they connect).
- **Government client:** private employer incorporated under the Canada Business Corporations Act (docs/discovery/hr-assistant.md §1); n/a: no federal institution, no AIA, no Ontario ministry or agency.

## System and intended purpose

- **What it does:** answers HR policy questions in French or English from published policies, takes leave requests and records them in UKG, and approves routine requests itself (R1, R2, R3).
- **Who uses it and who it affects:** distribution-centre staff in Montréal (1,150) and Toronto (640), pilot on one shift per centre for 6 weeks (docs/discovery/hr-assistant.md §1, §6); the Montréal staff are covered by a Teamsters collective agreement, Toronto staff are not unionised (docs/discovery/hr-assistant.md §5).
- **What the model decides and what code decides:** the model only extracts dates and leave type from the request; a code rule decides approval (D5, C3).
- **Effects it can cause:** writes an approved leave to UKG with approver "HR assistant" (C4); a wrong decision affects pay, scheduling and attendance records (docs/discovery/hr-assistant.md §4).
- **Human review of decisions about people:** none for auto-approved requests by design (C4); every other request reaches the manager's UKG queue (C5). Replay shows the rule approves 64% of pilot-shape requests without review (M2). Override rate and post-decision review: gap: not measured and no route recorded.

## Roles

- **Facts:** Érable commissions it and runs it for its staff (docs/discovery/hr-assistant.md §1); Southgate Labs built it and its engineers read logs during the pilot and support period (D4); Google Cloud hosts it and provides the model (D1, D2); Luc Tremblay decides (docs/discovery/hr-assistant.md §2). Contracts between these parties: gap: none recorded.
- **Australia, Privacy Act:** the employee records exemption is the client's and the references say it does not cover a contractor handling another organisation's employee information; whether Southgate Labs is an APP entity (turnover over $3 million, s 6D) is gap: turnover not recorded (counsel: confirm).
- **Canada:** Érable is the organisation responsible for the personal information under its control, including information handled by Southgate Labs and Google on its behalf (PIPEDA Schedule 4.1.3; Quebec service contract; canada.md reference, checked 2026-10-26). Whether Southgate Labs acts only for Érable or also for its own purposes (evaluation, product improvement) is counsel:. The Quebec person in charge is Marie-Claude Gagnon, Director, HR Operations (docs/discovery/hr-assistant.md §5); written delegation and website publication under s 3.1: gap: not recorded (counsel: confirm).

## Australia: Privacy Act and APPs

Scope: the consultancy's own handling only, because the client and the data subjects are in Canada (jurisdiction screen above; docs/discovery/hr-assistant.md §1).

- **No AI-specific regime:** Australia has no AI Act; obligations come from the laws screened here (checked 2026-10-26).
- **APPs engaged:** APP 11 (security and destruction) for Sydney engineers' access to logs with employee IDs, prompts and possibly health-related leave reasons (D3, D4, docs/discovery/hr-assistant.md §3); APP 3, 5 and 6 only if Southgate Labs collects or uses the information for its own purposes, for example evaluation sets replayed from July 2026 requests (M2; counsel: confirm). Detail in privacy-impact-input-pack.md.
- **Overseas disclosure (APP 8, s 16C):** n/a: Southgate Labs receives the data in Australia from Canada and no onward disclosure is recorded; gap: whether log extracts go to any tool outside Australia (D4; counsel: use or disclosure).
- **Notifiable data breaches:** if Southgate Labs is an APP entity, an eligible data breach is assessed within 30 days and notified as soon as practicable (checked 2026-10-26); which entity notifies whom: counsel:. Contract flow-down from Southgate Labs to Érable: gap: no contract recorded (security-questionnaire.md).
- **Pending, not law:** n/a: no tranche 2 or children's code item bears on a staff HR tool (docs/discovery/hr-assistant.md §3).

## Australia: Automated decisions (APP 1.7)

| Decision the agent touches | Solely or substantially and directly related | Human review and its measured share | Effect on the person | Personal information used | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| n/a: the client's decisions concern Canadian staff and the consultancy decides nothing about a person | n/a: APP 1.7 binds the entity making the decision, not the consultancy supplying the tool to a Canadian employer | n/a: see the Canada table for the review facts (C4, M2) | n/a: leave decision effects are recorded in the Canada table | n/a | docs/discovery/hr-assistant.md §1 |

- **Privacy policy inputs (APP 1.8):** n/a: no Australian entity makes a decision about a person here; Quebec notice facts are in system-card.md (C3, C4).

## Australia: Sector, state and government AI policy

- **Sector laws:** n/a: no Australian sector, health records or credit use; workplace surveillance notice rules concern Australian workplaces and none is monitored here (docs/discovery/hr-assistant.md §1).
- **Government AI policy:** n/a: private client, no Commonwealth or NSW agency (docs/discovery/hr-assistant.md §1).

## Canada: Privacy laws and roles

- **No AI-specific statute:** Canada has no AI Act; the Artificial Intelligence and Data Act died with Bill C-27 and Bill C-36 is not law (checked 2026-10-26). Bill C-36's second-reading status is reported; not confirmed at the source on 2026-10-26.
- **Which law governs each flow:** Quebec's Act covers Quebec employees; Ontario staff have no general private sector privacy statute for a provincially regulated employer, so the statute row is n/a: for Ontario, with counsel: on collective agreements, common law torts, human rights and employment standards, never as freedom from duties (canada.md reference, checked 2026-10-26).

| Flow (from the input pack's Data flows) | People and province | Law proposed | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Prompts and answers logged with employee ID for 60 days | Montréal staff (Quebec) | Quebec Act (counsel: which law) | D3, docs/discovery/hr-assistant.md §3 |
| Prompts and answers logged with employee ID for 60 days | Toronto staff (Ontario) | no general private sector statute (counsel: confirm; PIPEDA reaches employees only at federal works, Érable is provincially regulated) | D3, docs/discovery/hr-assistant.md §1 |
| Employee profile and leave data read from and written to UKG | both | Quebec Act for Montréal; counsel: for Toronto | R2, C4 |
| Model request to Gemini with US processing | both | Quebec s 17 for Montréal; counsel: for Toronto | D1 |
| Sydney engineers' log access | both | Quebec s 17 for Montréal; counsel: for Toronto | D4 |

- **Consent and appropriate purposes:** meaningful consent and the appropriate-purpose test, with express consent generally needed for sensitive information; leave reasons may mention health or family matters (docs/discovery/hr-assistant.md §3; privacy-impact-input-pack.md; counsel: whether employment necessity or consent covers each purpose). Never describe a lawful-basis analysis here.
- **Cross-border and out-of-Quebec flows:** Quebec s 17 assessment and written agreement before any flow leaves Quebec, including the rest of Canada (transfer-assessment.md; D1, D2, D4; counsel: adequate protection). Alberta country list: n/a: no Alberta staff recorded (docs/discovery/hr-assistant.md §1).
- **Breach clocks and records:** PIPEDA as soon as feasible and a 24-month record of every breach; Quebec notice to the CAI and the person on a risk of serious injury and an incident register; Alberta and BC: n/a: no staff there (security-questionnaire.md; checked 2026-10-26).

## Canada: Automated decisions

| Decision the agent touches | Exclusive automation (Quebec s 12.1) | Review route and measured share | Explanation the design can produce | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Approval of a leave request under two days, balance sufficient, no blackout date | Proposed yes: code rule decides, approver recorded as "HR assistant", no human review (C3, C4, D5); counsel: does s 12.1 apply, and does it cover an approval | None for approvals by design; 64% of pilot-shape requests would be approved this way (M2); post-decision review route: gap: not recorded | The three rule conditions (duration, balance, blackout) could be reported; no contract produces or logs the reasons for a decision: gap | C3, C4, M2, D5 |
| Any other request, including every request of two days or more | Proposed no: routed to the manager's UKG queue where a person decides (C5, C3 failure outcome) | Manager decides; share and time: gap: not measured | The manager's own reasons | C5 |

- **Duties if s 12.1 applies (as reported; not confirmed at the source on 2026-10-26):** tell the person no later than when the decision is communicated; on request give the personal information used, the reasons and principal factors, and the correction right; let the person submit observations to a staff member able to review the decision. The record holds none of the three: gap: proposed goals for adk-operational-guardrails and the Érable HR owner.
- **Counsel questions specific to this design:** the rule decides, but a model extracts the dates and leave type (D5, M3 98.4% correct on 500 replayed requests), so a wrong extraction changes the decision; whether that is one automated process is counsel:. The brief says staff may not know a request was decided without a person (docs/discovery/hr-assistant.md §4).
- **Federal client:** n/a: not a federal institution (docs/discovery/hr-assistant.md §1).

## Canada: Employment, sector and government AI policy

- **Employment:** Ontario electronic monitoring policy: Érable has well over 25 employees in Ontario (640 in Toronto, docs/discovery/hr-assistant.md §1) and prompts are logged against employee IDs for 60 days (D3), a fact for that written policy (canada.md reference, checked 2026-10-26; counsel: does the log engage the policy, and is an update needed now). Ontario job-posting AI disclosure: n/a: the assistant does not screen applicants (R1 to R4). Human rights codes and employment standards for leave, including accommodation of health and family leave: counsel: named, not analysed here, and the Quebec Act respecting labour standards and the Ontario Employment Standards Act are not covered by this pack's references. The Montréal collective agreement in force may govern leave approval and monitoring (docs/discovery/hr-assistant.md §5; counsel: consultation duty and any grievance exposure).
- **Quebec language law:** counsel: whether the Charter of the French Language requires French notices, interfaces or documents for this system; this pack's references do not cover it (R1 provides French and English answers).
- **Sector and consumer:** n/a: PHIPA, CASL and the Competition Act are not engaged by an internal staff tool with no outbound messages or public claims (R1 to R4; counsel: confirm PHIPA is not engaged by leave reasons).
- **Government client:** n/a: private client (docs/discovery/hr-assistant.md §1).

## Applicable dates

| Regime | Obligation | Applies from | Relevance here |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Canada (Quebec) | s 3.3 privacy impact assessment for an information system project | 22 September 2023 (CAI aide-mémoire, checked 2026-10-26) | Needed before the pilot starts; W3 |
| Canada (Quebec) | s 17 assessment before communication outside Quebec | 22 September 2023 (CAI aide-mémoire, checked 2026-10-26) | Three flows leave Quebec (D1, D2, D4); W4 |
| Canada (Quebec) | s 12.1 automated decisions | 22 September 2023 (CAI aide-mémoire, checked 2026-10-26; wording reported; not confirmed at the source on 2026-10-26) | C3, C4 for Montréal staff |
| Australia | APP 1.7 transparency for automated decisions | 10 December 2026 (OAIC fact sheet, checked 2026-10-26) | n/a: no Australian entity makes the decision; the pilot decision is 2026-11-24 and the pilot spans this date (docs/discovery/hr-assistant.md §6) |

- **AI literacy and staff training:** gap: no training or guidance for pilot staff or managers recorded (proposed goal for the Érable HR owner).
- **Documents the client's own process produces:** the Quebec EFVP under s 3.3, owned by Marie-Claude Gagnon, wait W3; the s 17 assessment and written agreement, owned by Érable with Me Geneviève Roy, wait W4; the Ontario electronic monitoring policy update if counsel says so, conditional wait W6; consultation with the Montréal Teamsters local if the collective agreement requires it, conditional wait W5; counsel's review of this pack, wait W2.

## Questions for counsel

1. counsel: Does the Quebec Act govern Érable's handling of Montréal staff leave data and prompts? Regime Canada; facts D3, docs/discovery/hr-assistant.md §1; needed before W3.
2. counsel: Is the auto-approval a decision "based exclusively on automated processing" under s 12.1, given a deterministic rule decides and a model only extracts the dates (D5, C3, C4)? Needed before the pilot decision (W2).
3. counsel: Does s 12.1 cover a favourable decision (an approval)? The reported text is silent (canada.md reference, not confirmed at the source on 2026-10-26). Needed before W2.
4. counsel: If s 12.1 applies, what notice, explanation and review route must exist, and is a manager route (C5) enough as the staff member who reviews? Needed before the pilot starts.
5. counsel: Does a s 17 assessment show adequate protection for Toronto, the United States and Australia, and is the Google Cloud agreement, or a Southgate Labs contract, the required written agreement? Facts D1, D2, D4; needed before W4.
6. counsel: Which law governs the Toronto staff flows (no general private sector statute, PIPEDA for cross-border flows, or common law)? Facts D1, D4.
7. counsel: Does Southgate Labs act only for Érable, or also for its own purposes (evaluation from replayed July 2026 requests, M2)? Needed before the replay data is retained.
8. counsel: Is Southgate Labs an APP entity, and does the Privacy Act reach its handling of Canadian staff data in Sydney (D4)?
9. counsel: Does prompt logging with employee IDs (D3) engage the Ontario electronic monitoring policy now, and does it engage any term of the Montréal collective agreement? Needed before the pilot starts (W5, W6).
10. counsel: Does the Charter of the French Language require French notices, interface or documents for this system?
11. counsel: Does a leave reason about health or family make the data sensitive for consent and for the Quebec s 3.3 assessment, and is screening before the model call required (docs/discovery/hr-assistant.md §3; no screening evidence recorded)?
12. counsel: What do the Quebec Act respecting labour standards, the Ontario Employment Standards Act and human rights codes require of leave decisions, including a duty to accommodate (not analysed in this pack)?

Assumptions proceeded on (non-interactive run): assumption: consultancy home Australia (default); assumption: "out of scope: leave of two days or more" (docs/architecture/hr-assistant.md Scope gate) means not auto-decided, since R4 and C3 send them to the manager; assumption: Érable's Quebec head office makes Montréal staff data an enterprise's data under the Quebec Act; assumption: no contracts exist beyond what the design records, because none are recorded.
